sentences.en: This is really a two-hour presentation I give to high school students, cut down to three minutes.
sentences.zh: 后来我下了飞机，来到TED忽然间我想到，天啊，我置身于一屋子成功人士之中！

sentences.en: And it all started one day on a plane, on my way to TED, seven years ago.
sentences.zh: 忽然间我想到，天啊，我置身于一屋子成功人士之中！为什么我不问问他们是怎样走向成功的呢。

sentences.en: And in the seat next to me was a high school student, a teenager, and she came from a really poor family.
sentences.zh: 为什么我不问问他们是怎样走向成功的呢。这样我就可以把答案告诉孩子们了。所以就这样，7年中我坐了500次采访。现在我就要告诉你们是什么带来了成功

sentences.en: And she wanted to make something of her life, and she asked me a simple little question.
sentences.zh: 现在我就要告诉你们是什么带来了成功是什么启发了TED演讲者们。第一点是激情

sentences.en: She said, "What leads to success?" And I felt really badly, because I couldn't give her a good answer.
sentences.zh: 第一点是激情Freeman Thomas 说：“我总是被我的热情所牵引着”TED的讲演者因为有爱才做事情，不是为了钱。

sentences.en: So I get off the plane, and I come to TED.
sentences.zh: TED的讲演者因为有爱才做事情，不是为了钱。

sentences.en: And I think, jeez, I'm in the middle of a room of successful people!

sentences.en: So why don't I ask them what helped them succeed, and pass it on to kids?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是如果你是为了爱而做的，钱自然而然就来了。刻苦！Rupert Murdoch 曾经告诉过我 “都是刻苦“ 为努力”

sentences.en: So here we are, seven years, 500 interviews later, and I'm going to tell you what really leads to success and makes TEDsters tick.
sentences.zh: 刻苦！Rupert Murdoch 曾经告诉过我 “都是刻苦“ 为努力”“天下没有白吃的午餐。但是我得到了很多乐趣。”他提到了乐趣？？Rupert？是的！

sentences.en: And the first thing is passion. Freeman Thomas says, "I'm driven by my passion."
sentences.zh: TED讲演者都有一份充满乐趣的工作，而且他们都很刻苦。我觉得，他们都不是工作狂，他们是享受工作狂

sentences.en: TEDsters do it for love; they don't do it for money.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，他们都不是工作狂，他们是享受工作狂精通！Alex Garden说：”要想成功，就要真的深入其中“

sentences.en: Carol Coletta says, "I would pay someone to do what I do."
sentences.zh: 精通！Alex Garden说：”要想成功，就要真的深入其中“

sentences.en: And the interesting thing is: if you do it for love, the money comes anyway.
sentences.zh: 精通！Alex Garden说：”要想成功，就要真的深入其中““然后做到精通。”想要做到精通没有秘诀，就是练习，练习，再练习。

sentences.en: Work! Rupert Murdoch said to me, "It's all hard work.
sentences.zh: 想要做到精通没有秘诀，就是练习，练习，再练习。还有就是专注。Norman Jewison 告诉过我，

sentences.en: Did he say fun? Rupert? Yes! (Laughter) TEDsters do have fun working. And they work hard.

sentences.en: I figured, they're not workaholics. They're workafrolics.
sentences.zh: “心灵上，神情上。你一定要强迫，强迫，强迫。”“你要强迫自己去战胜羞涩和自我怀疑”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Good! (Applause) Alex Garden says, "To be successful, put your nose down in something and get damn good at it."
sentences.zh: “你要强迫自己去战胜羞涩和自我怀疑”Goldie Hawn说：“我总是怀疑自己。怀疑自己不够优秀，不用聪明。我从不相信我会成功。”想要成功地强迫自己并不总容易，

sentences.en: I didn't think I'd make it." Now it's not always easy to push yourself, and that's why they invented mothers.

sentences.en: A lot of kids want to be millionaires. The first thing I say is: "OK, well you can't serve yourself; you've got to serve others something of value.
sentences.zh: 而且我可以举出很多证据。坚持。Joe Kraus 说”恒心是我们成功地第一条原因。“”你必须坚持度过失败，你必须坚持度过crap“

sentences.en: Because that's the way people really get rich."

sentences.en: Ideas! TEDster Bill Gates says, "I had an idea: founding the first micro-computer software company."
sentences.zh: ”这里的crap是指”批评，拒绝，卑鄙小人和压力““（大笑）所以，这个问题的答案很简单：

sentences.en: I'd say it was a pretty good idea. And there's no magic to creativity in coming up with ideas -- it's just doing some very simple things.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个问题的答案很简单：付4000块来TED会场。如果不能来，就做到以上八点---相信我，

sentences.en: And I give lots of evidence. Persist! Joe Kraus says, "Persistence is the number one reason for our success."
sentences.zh: 如果不能来，就做到以上八点---相信我，这重要的八点就是通向成功的秘诀。谢谢TED讲演者参与我的采访！

sentences.en: Which of course means "Criticism, Rejection, Assholes and Pressure."

sentences.en: (Laughter) So, the answer to this question is simple: Pay 4,000 bucks and come to TED.

sentences.en: (Laughter) Or failing that, do the eight things -- and trust me, these are the big eight things that lead to success.
sentences.zh: （笑声）或者做不到这一点，就做八件事——相信我，这些是通往成功的八件事。
